[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The Lambda permission :resource.aws_lambda_permission.cur_per_service uses a literal function name, so Terraform does not ensure module :module.cur_per_service has created the function before the permission is added. Reference the module's function ARN/name to establish this dependency.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The Lambda permission `:resource.aws_lambda_permission.cur_per_service` uses a literal function name and can be created before the Lambda in `:module.cur_per_service`; Lambda must exist before AWS can attach its invoke permission.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
This permission uses a locally constructed function name that matches the function created by this module, but it does not reference the module output. It can therefore be created before the Lambda function exists, causing the permission API call to fail; wire the function name to the module output to establish ordering.

----------------------------------------

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
aws_lambda_permission.cur_per_service sets `function_name = local.cur_per_service_lambda_name`, an interpolated string that does not reference the Lambda module. Terraform therefore sees no edge to module.cur_per_service and may call AddPermission before the function exists, which fails with ResourceNotFoundException. The permission must be created after the function.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
`aws_lambda_permission.cur_per_service` sets `function_name = local.cur_per_service_lambda_name`, a plain string, so it only depends on `aws_s3_bucket.aws_billing_report` (via `source_arn`) and is not ordered after `module.cur_per_service`. The permission can be created before the function exists, failing with ResourceNotFoundException. Reference the module output to establish the dependency implicitly.

The S3 notification :resource.aws_s3_bucket_notification.cur_notification configures the :module.cur_per_resource_process Lambda target but does not wait for its S3 invoke permission :resource.aws_lambda_permission.cur_per_resource_process. S3 notification setup must follow creation of the corresponding Lambda permission.

----------------------------------------

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The S3 bucket notification configures an invocation for the per-resource-process Lambda, but it does not wait for that function's S3 invoke permission. AWS validates Lambda permissions when installing bucket notifications, so this permission must be created first.

----------------------------------------

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
aws_s3_bucket_notification.cur_notification declares three `lambda_function` blocks (cur_per_service, cur_per_resource, cur_per_resource_process) but its `depends_on` only covers aws_lambda_permission.cur_per_service and aws_lambda_permission.cur_per_resource. The third lambda_function block references module.cur_per_resource_process, so the aws_lambda_permission.cur_per_resource_process statement may not exist yet when PutBucketNotificationConfiguration validates the destination, causing "Unable to validate the following destination configurations".

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
`aws_s3_bucket_notification.cur_notification` has three `lambda_function` blocks but its `depends_on` only lists `aws_lambda_permission.cur_per_service` and `aws_lambda_permission.cur_per_resource`. The third destination, `module.cur_per_resource_process` (filter_prefix "tmp/cur-per-resource/"), has no such ordering, and a module reference does not imply its `aws_lambda_permission`. S3 validates the invoke permission when applying `PutBucketNotificationConfiguration`, so this can fail with "Unable to validate the following destination configurations". Add `aws_lambda_permission.cur_per_resource_process` to `depends_on`.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
aws_s3_bucket_notification.cur_notification declares three lambda_function blocks — module.cur_per_service, module.cur_per_resource and module.cur_per_resource_process — but its depends_on only lists aws_lambda_permission.cur_per_service and aws_lambda_permission.cur_per_resource. The PutBucketNotificationConfiguration call validates that every destination Lambda grants s3.amazonaws.com invoke permission, so the third block (prefix "tmp/cur-per-resource/") must also be applied after aws_lambda_permission.cur_per_resource_process; otherwise the very first apply fails with "Unable to validate the following destination configurations". Add it to depends_on (there is no attribute on the notification that can reference the permission, so a bare depends_on is the correct fix).

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
aws_s3_bucket_notification.cur_notification configures an S3 trigger for the cur_per_resource_process lambda, but its depends_on only lists aws_lambda_permission.cur_per_service and aws_lambda_permission.cur_per_resource — aws_lambda_permission.cur_per_resource_process is omitted. AWS validates that S3 is allowed to invoke each target function when the notification configuration is applied, so creating the notification before that permission exists fails.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
aws_s3_bucket_notification.cur_notification configures a lambda_function trigger for the per-resource-process function (module.cur_per_resource_process) but its depends_on only lists aws_lambda_permission.cur_per_service and aws_lambda_permission.cur_per_resource — it omits aws_lambda_permission.cur_per_resource_process. S3 validates the invoke permission when PutBucketNotificationConfiguration is applied; if the notification is created before that permission exists, apply fails with "Unable to validate the following destination configurations". An explicit depends_on on the missing permission is required.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
aws_s3_bucket_notification.cur_notification configures a lambda_function destination for module.cur_per_resource_process but its depends_on omits aws_lambda_permission.cur_per_resource_process (it only lists the permissions for cur_per_service and cur_per_resource). S3 validates the invoke permission for every Lambda destination when applying the notification configuration, so this permission must exist first or apply fails.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The export :resource.aws_bcmdataexports_export.cur_per_resource writes to the billing bucket, but it can be created before :resource.aws_s3_bucket_policy.cur_bucket_policy grants the BCM Data Exports service access required for delivery. Add an explicit dependency on the bucket policy.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The export `:resource.aws_bcmdataexports_export.cur_per_resource` targets the billing bucket but has no ordering dependency on its policy `:resource.aws_s3_bucket_policy.cur_bucket_policy`, which grants BCM Data Exports the required bucket access. Ensure the policy is attached before configuring the export.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The BCM Data Exports export writes to this S3 bucket, whose policy grants the bcm-data-exports.amazonaws.com service access. Ensure the bucket policy is installed before creating the export; the bucket reference alone does not establish that ordering.

----------------------------------------

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
aws_bcmdataexports_export.cur_per_resource writes to the aws_billing_report bucket and requires the bucket policy granting `bcm-data-exports.amazonaws.com` (statement `EnableAWSDataExportsToWriteToS3AndCheckPolicy`) to already exist. Data Exports validates write access to the destination bucket when the export is created, so without an ordering edge to aws_s3_bucket_policy.cur_bucket_policy the create can fail with Access Denied. The graph only shows a dependency on aws_s3_bucket.aws_billing_report.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
`aws_bcmdataexports_export.cur_per_resource` points its `s3_destination` at `aws_s3_bucket.aws_billing_report`, so it only waits for the bucket. The `bcm-data-exports.amazonaws.com` principal permissions (s3:PutObject / s3:GetBucketPolicy) are granted by `aws_s3_bucket_policy.cur_bucket_policy`, which Terraform may create after the export, causing export creation/validation to fail. Order the export after the bucket policy.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
aws_bcmdataexports_export.cur_per_resource creates a BCM Data Exports export that delivers into aws_s3_bucket.aws_billing_report, which is only writable by bcm-data-exports.amazonaws.com because of aws_s3_bucket_policy.cur_bucket_policy (the "EnableAWSDataExportsToWriteToS3AndCheckPolicy" statement). The export depends on the bucket but has no ordering against the bucket policy, and AWS validates the destination bucket's policy when the export is created, so a fresh apply can fail while the policy has not yet been attached. Order the export after aws_s3_bucket_policy.cur_bucket_policy.

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
aws_bcmdataexports_export.cur_per_resource writes to aws_s3_bucket.aws_billing_report, but the export's creation is validated by AWS against the destination bucket's policy (the policy document's "EnableAWSDataExportsToWriteToS3AndCheckPolicy" statement grants bcm-data-exports.amazonaws.com s3:PutObject/s3:GetBucketPolicy for exactly this). The export only implicitly references the bucket, not aws_s3_bucket_policy.cur_bucket_policy; if the export is created before the bucket policy is applied, the destination-access validation can fail. It should depend on the bucket policy.

----------------------------------------

The export must be created after the bucket policy is in place.
